video_title: Boogie & Lou Debate If Steph Curry Is Top 10 All-Time!

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on Steph Curry's unexpected dominance this season
quotes.excerpt: He's 38 years old and he's looking like he's in his prime 25 years old maybe.
quotes.quote: I don't think anybody expected this Warriors group to come out and play the way they've been playing this season so far. Obviously, the key catalyst of all of this is Steph Curry. He's playing out of his mind right now. He's 38 years old and he's looking like he's in his prime 25 years old maybe. He's looking incredible out there, he's leading this group. This is very unexpected, but this is also what I was looking for when it came to Steph Curry. I said it before, he has too much greatness left in his game for him not to be playing high-level basketball and still being must-watch TV.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on the Warriors' surprising early season success
quotes.excerpt: This should put teams on notice that maybe these guys that stay three or four years.
quotes.quote: It's interesting because at the beginning of the season we were talking about them possibly being a play-in team, treading water till Jimmy gets back. We didn't know the status of Kristaps Porzingis, and they've blown all expectations. It's still very early, but the rookie has been incredible. People thought Mike Dunleavy was crazy for taking him this early just because of his age and how long he was in school. This should put teams on notice that maybe these guys that stay three or four years are more ready to help a team like a rookie right now to step right in, who's been through all the rigors of college basketball. And then Steph Curry, we always say you always have a chance to win with him on the floor. He's taking that to the next level.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on the Warriors' potential to remain competitive
quotes.excerpt: Anytime you got a Steph Curry led team and the way that he's playing.
quotes.quote: A lot of basketball to be played. A lot of teams are having success early on. That's going to be tough for me to say. Listen, what Boogie just said, anytime you got a Steph Curry led team and the way that he's playing, you always have an opportunity to win at a high clip. However, what's the name of the game? Staying healthy. If they can get a Jimmy Butler back, if they can get him back, they've proven to be exactly what Draymond said. He looks like he's going to be one of their next franchise leaders, somebody that you can trust and rely on. They got a good thing going right now. I don't know about titles. It's a feel-good story right now for Golden State with the record that they have, but you still got some top dogs out there that's younger, that's deeper, and at this point, recently, a little bit more experienced.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Michelle Beadle and Lou Williams on Steph Curry's status as a must-watch player
quotes.excerpt: If you pay to go see Steph Curry, you're not leaving disappointed.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I can't believe that at 38 years old, is he still the must-see ticket?

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Absolutely. Like I said, he's playing at a level right now where it looks like he's 25, 26 years old. He's always been one of the game's best showmen. When the lights come on, you know he's going to bring it every single night. He's must-watch TV. He's a pioneer in the modern-day game. So, absolutely, he'll always be must-watch TV until he decides to hang up his sneakers.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Steph Curry reaching his 'flow state'
quotes.excerpt: Steph Curry has reached his flow state. He know exactly where he's going to shoot the ball.
quotes.quote: You have guys in their careers that they reach their prime and they're playing at a crazy pace and then right after that, they reach a flow state. Steph Curry has reached his flow state. He know exactly where he's going to shoot the ball, he know exactly what he's capable of, he trust his training and everything. Some of the things that we are amazed that he does, it's regular. Even his pre-game warm-up that he shoots the ball from the damn tunnel, he does that every game. I'm like, bro, I don't know if I can sink one of those in a season. That's something that he does on a daily basis. That's average to him. He's reached a flow state in his game where it's incredible to watch.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Steph Curry's legacy and rewriting history
quotes.excerpt: Steph Curry is somebody that's been able to rewrite history along with some of the other pioneers.
quotes.quote: There comes guys that come along where they rewrite history. Steph Curry is somebody that's been able to rewrite history along with some of the other pioneers in our game from the early 2010s and on up. These guys have been tremendous. Steph Curry has been tremendous. He was able to accomplish all of these things with none of this being in the expectation level by the way. Maybe some All-Stars, maybe some first teams. He's been able to carve out four NBA championships, a Finals MVP, a league MVP. He rewrote the way that we play the game as pros. He rewrote the game how the youth play the game with so many three-pointers in the game. He's been able to rewrite history every step of the way.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins' top point guards of all-time list
quotes.excerpt: The top three to four for me would obviously be Magic, Steph, Isaiah Thomas.
quotes.quote: The top three to four for me would obviously be Magic, Steph, Isaiah Thomas. And you got to throw Oscar Robertson in there somewhere. After that, it kind of gets a little shaky. It's a lot of guys you can consider. Obviously, you got the Steve Nashes, the Jason Kidds, the Tony Parkers, the Chris Pauls of the world. So it's a lot of options to kind of round out that top five, but I think for the top three, top four, I think those guys are kind of solidified in history.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on why he prioritizes modern players in his rankings
quotes.excerpt: I'm only the reason I'm fighting for our guys is because Isaiah Thomas came on this show.
quotes.quote: I'm only the reason I'm fighting for our guys is because Isaiah Thomas came on this show and he told us we need to start talking about our legends in a different way. And since then, I understand because you know what, some of these guys in the 80s and the 90s, they not going to give us the same respect as we are giving them. So we should crown our guys that we saw play, that we competed against, that changed the trajectory of our careers on a nightly basis based on how they played and we got to give them their proper respects and their flowers. So a five for me, Magic Johnson for sure, Isaiah Thomas for sure, Steph Curry for sure. And then we can start rounding the list out from some Russell Westbrooks to some Chris Pauls, some Oscar Robertsons, some Steve Nashes, some Jason Kidds. Then we start having those conversations. We got to even consider Shaq at this point.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on his personal top 10 point guard rankings
quotes.excerpt: To me Steph Curry is the greatest point guard of all time.
quotes.quote: If I ranked my top 10 players that I've seen with my eyes, I might not put those three in there. Now I might play the game and be a history buff and throw them in there just to sound like everyone else. But if I'm going with my eyes and what I know, like Larry Bird versus Kevin Durant, I'm a Kevin Durant guy. Like I really am. So my list will look wildly different than most people. To me Steph Curry is the greatest point guard of all time. What he did with shooting the basketball off the catch, off the dribble, off screens, like I've never seen anyone in the history of the planet do that regardless of position. Steph Curry to me has to be in there. So if Kevin Durant's in our top 10 who I love, Steph Curry has to be. So now we're really weeding some guys out. To me is the most dominant player ever in the history of the planet so he's got to be in there. And then we're talking MJ, LeBron, Kobe.
